key_insight: Energy-cost-only HEMS optimisation can hide large battery degradation costs, making apparent savings misleading and sometimes far smaller than the true lifecycle expense.
engineering_relevance: For residential PV-battery systems, controllers should account for degradation explicitly, because ignoring it can produce economically poor operating schedules even when energy bills look lower.
method: Receding-horizon mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) baseline for a UK residential HEMS
3×3 sensitivity study over three battery sizes and three PV array sizes
Post-hoc degradation estimation using the Naumann stress model with rainflow cycle counting
evidence_signal: Using REFIT residential demand data, the study found degradation cost stayed constant for each battery size and could exceed energy cost savings by up to 1,060%.
watch_item: The degradation cost was estimated after optimisation rather than included directly in the control objective, so real-world performance may differ once degradation-aware constraints are enforced.
paper_title: Hidden Degradation Costs in Energy-Cost-Only HEMS Optimisation: Study on Battery and PV Sensitivity
